summary: Submitted sourced research feedback recording the strongest consequence of the confirmed snapshot-ordering defect, with a new SourceRange S-api-newraft-scan (api.go:598-608). Two consequences follow from restoring the lower-index snapshot: first, restoreSnapshot tries snapshots in List order and keeps the first that loads, setting lastApplied/lastSnapshot from it, so an inversely ordered retained pair makes the node adopt the older state (regressing applied state until a leader re-supplies the range); second, the configuration scan that follows walks from the restored snapshot index to the last log index calling GetLog for every index and panics on a missing one, and a hole in that range is exactly what a previous user restore leaves behind (it burns the index above the last log and appends only above it). The lower-index choice enables both: with the contract-conformant ordering the higher snapshot index would cover the hole. The only unestablished link is the coexistence of an inversely ordered retained pair with a user-restore hole, so this is recorded as a sourced hypothesis and a consequence of the same confirmed responsibility rather than promoted to a new claim; the feedback also lists the remaining unread areas (tcp transport and pipeline pooling, FSM batch manager, testing helpers). No map change is proposed. Preflight returned valid:true; the run's five confirmed_in_scope conclusions across six implementation_reproduced findings are unchanged.
